simple: a list of "at this time, break this" lines that a test follows exactly.
analogy: a fire-drill plan that says which door is locked at which minute.
precise: a data file of timed fault steps (crash, restart, isolate, partition, heal) with targets resolved at run time, such as "the current leader", plus network settings and a seed; with the seed it determines a simulated run completely.
source: R1 of MP2 (lab run; the definition is this course's)

simple: how often your tests notice a bug you put in on purpose.
analogy: hiding a few known mistakes in an exam to see whether the marker finds them.
precise: for each deliberately broken variant (mutant) of a system, the fraction of test runs in which at least one check fails; a variant never caught survives and is either a gap in the tests or shown to be harmless under the options used.
source: R2 of MP2 (lab run; the definition is this course's)

simple: one number that summarises everything that happened in a test run.
analogy: a photograph of the finished notebook pages, to compare two runs at a glance.
precise: a hash (FNV-1a in the MP2 starter) over the client history and every server's final term, commit index and log; equal fingerprints for two runs of one seed are evidence that the harness is deterministic.

simple: a test write sent once everything is repaired, to check the system works again.
analogy: after the storm, posting one letter to see whether the mail runs.
precise: from the settle time of a run (network healed, crashed servers restarted), a write sent to the current leader at fixed intervals until one is answered; the run fails its liveness check if none is answered before the end, and the delay to the first answer is the recovery time.
source: R1 of MP2 (lab run; the definition is this course's)

simple: servers keep starting elections although nothing is broken.
analogy: friends who keep calling a new vote because the organiser's postcard arrives a day after they expect it.
precise: repeated leader elections in a consensus cluster without faults, caused by timing settings (a heartbeat interval not well below the election timeout) or by disruptive servers; safety holds, availability falls.
source: R4 and D1 of MP2 (pending verification)

simple: the rules of your system, written down before the code.
analogy: the club's rulebook that every friend can check a decision against.
precise: a document giving each role's state, every message and its fields, every handler as preconditions and effects, the persistence points, the client contract and the invariants the tests check; reviewed at a design gate before implementation.
source: D6 of MP2 (the MP2 card names it as a deliverable; the section list is this course's proposal)

simple: the service remembers each client's last request number so a retry is not done twice.
analogy: numbering your letters so the friend can throw away a copy that arrives twice.
precise: per-client state kept in the replicated state machine (last applied request number and its reply) that makes retried commands take effect at most once, so a client may safely retry after an unknown outcome.

simple: a worker that was given up for dead but is still running the job.
analogy: a friend cut off by a storm who keeps doing a chore that was already given to someone else.
precise: a scheduler worker that was partitioned rather than crashed, so its job is re-placed and runs twice; the defences are idempotent jobs or a fencing token checked by the resource the job writes to.
